summary: Intermittent dtype conversion and batch reshuffle causing nondeterministic rerank top-k and latency spikes
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports nondeterministic reranking results and periodic latency spikes for batched embedding->rerank flows. Problem appears when they send mixed-precision embedding requests from multiple app instances: top-k ordering flips on otherwise-identical queries and some batches take 3-4x longer to complete.

Impact:
- Customer-facing search endpoints for BrightDocs are returning inconsistent ranked results visible to end users.
- Tail latency spikes to ~2.5s (baseline ~400ms) causing user-facing timeouts.

Environment:
- prod (us-east), BrightDocs account (enterprise).
- Models: redwood-embed-v3, redwood-rerank-v1.

Steps to reproduce provided by customer:
1) Construct a 32-item batch where half items originate from an older app instance posting float32 embeddings and half from a new instance posting float16.
2) Hit the rerank endpoint with top_k=10, request streaming.
3) Repeat identical payloads and observe occasional top-k permutation and tail latency for the same batch IDs.

Observed behavior:
- Non-deterministic top-k permutations between runs for identical payloads.
- Tail latency spikes correlate with batches containing mixed dtype embeddings.
- Service logs show warnings about implicit dtype casting and occasional fallback to CPU execution paths.

Expected behavior:
- Deterministic rerank order for identical payloads and stable latency regardless of client-side dtype variance; server should normalize or reject mixed-dtype transparently.
comments: 2026-03-12 09:18 - Aisha Patel: Ticket opened after call with BrightDocs. They attached sample payloads and timeline. Assigned to SRE on-call for triage.
2026-03-12 10:05 - Marco Chen: Acknowledged. Reproduced locally with mixed-precision batch construction. Will enable debug logs on embeddings-service canary in us-east and collect traces.
2026-03-12 14:42 - Sofia Ramirez (BrightDocs): We observe top-k flips ~15% of runs; impacts 'most relevant' results. Please advise ETA.

2026-03-13 08:30 - Marco Chen: Investigation underway. Hypothesis: ingestion path implicitly upcasts mixed dtypes triggering CPU normalization and numerical differences that affect tie-breaking. Added a canary metric for 'mixed-dtype-batch' rate.

2026-03-13 14:10 - Ethan Cole (serving-runtime): Found that normalize_and_cast path uses a parallel memcopy with a nondeterministic ordering into the micro-batcher buffer; reproduced nondeterministic reorder in unit test.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-13: Repro script created (scripts/repro/mixed_dtype_rerank.sh) confirming nondeterministic top-k and latency tail with mixed dtypes.

Root cause hypothesis: Mixed-dtype batches trigger an upcast to float32 then an in-place memcopy into a pooling buffer. The multithreaded memcopy has a race that occasionally reshuffles the item order before KV assignment, changing similarity computations and rerank tie resolution.
Secondary effect: Float32 promotion forces a GPU-to-CPU fallback for certain quantized kernels, causing affected batches to execute on CPU with ~3-4x latency.
Telemetry: 0.8% of total batches in us-east flagged mixed-dtype in last 24h; BrightDocs accounts for ~12% mixed-dtype during their staged SDK rollout.
Temporary mitigation: Canary gate that rejects mixed-dtype requests with 400 and guidance to upgrade SDK; removed after customer impact complaints.
Test gaps: No existing unit/integration tests cover mixed-dtype ingestion stability or copy ordering behavior.
Repro notes: Issue reproduces when multiple client worker processes interleave sends; homogeneous single-source batches are stable.
resolution:
Hotfix deployed 2026-03-14: embeddings-service PR #408 enforces deterministic normalization for mixed-dtype batches by performing an index-stable single-threaded cast into a preallocated GPU buffer prior to micro-batcher assembly and adding an explicit per-batch ordering tag. Deployed to canary then rolled to prod in us-east. SDK team published client warning in 1.4.3 recommending stable dtype and optional 'X-Embed-Dtype' header.

Follow-ups:
- INT-2133: add unit/integration tests for mixed-dtype ingestion and memcopy ordering.
- INT-2134: add telemetry alert when a single customer's mixed-dtype rate exceeds 1%.
- Update Confluence runbook with recovery steps and SDK guidance.

Customer update: BrightDocs confirmed hotfix on staging and began phased production validation. Monitoring shows top-k stability and tail latency returned to baseline.
